messages:
maria_support: Customer (acct=acme-inc) escalated intermittent streaming failures on hosted API. They see client-side errors (broken pipe) and our gateway logs a 502; billing spikes flagged as 5xx. Repro steps attached by the customer below.

lisa_support: I opened PROD-9876 and attached their logs + request ids: req=req-0a1b2c3d, trace=trace-9f8e7d. Customer says it happens mostly on long responses (>30s) with chunked encoding.

jon_eng_runtime: Sounds like a downstream (client) half-close while we still write. When our runtime writes after the client FIN we see EPIPE, the proxy currently translates that into a 502 and billing counts it as server 5xx. Need to distinguish client-abort vs real server error.

kevin_sre: Can you paste the gateway/runtime log lines for that req? Also capture TCP FIN timing with tcpdump so we can prove directionality.

maria_support: Pasting sanitized logs from the gateway (timestamps UTC):

```
[2026-03-15T14:12:23Z] req=req-0a1b2c3d gateway: write failed: broken pipe (EPIPE) downstream=203.0.113.45:51234 upstream=runtime-03:8080
[2026-03-15T14:12:23Z] req=req-0a1b2c3d gateway: returning 502 to client, billing_category=5xx
[2026-03-15T14:12:23Z] req=req-0a1b2c3d runtime-03: stream write error: write tcp 10.0.0.12:8080->203.0.113.45:51234: write: broken pipe
```

jon_eng_runtime: Thanks — that matches a write() -> EPIPE from runtime. Repro I used locally: I start a simple streaming server that emits many chunks, then a test client that closes the socket after 2 chunks.

Repro notes (staging):
```
# server: emits chunked payloads slowly
curl -N -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" -d @payload.json https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/streams
# client abort script (python) closes connection after N chunks
python abort_client.py --after-chunks 2 --url "https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/streams"
```

Result: gateway logs the same EPIPE pattern and issues 502; billing hook increments 5xx counter.

kevin_sre: Proposed next steps: 1) capture pcap on proxy/runtime to confirm client FIN before write; 2) add a short-term metric to track write-failures with downstream FIN timing; 3) adjust billing classification to treat confirmed client-aborts as non-billable 5xx (or special category).

maria_support: Customer asked for a workaround while we investigate. Suggested changing client to smaller chunk sizes and enabling TCP keepalive; they tried reducing chunk size and saw fewer failures.

jon_eng_runtime: Quick technical proposal: when runtime gets EPIPE on write, check recent socket state for a FIN/FIN-ACK from client. If FIN is present within a 200ms window before write failure, classify as client-abort and do not surface as internal 5xx in billing. I will open a PR to add this heuristic to gateway's error handler and emit a new metric streaming.client_abort_count.

sam_billing: Heads-up — if we reclassify historical events we need a list of affected req ids to consider invoice adjustments. pls collect IDs for the last 30 days where write-fail + upstream status==502.

kevin_sre: For proof, run tcpdump on the gateway node: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/req-req-0a1b2c3d.pcap host 203.0.113.45 and then grep logs for req id. Also LD_PRELOAD debug trick to log write() errno if needed.

jon_eng_runtime: I'll push a staging build with both the detection heuristic and additional logging (socket state + time delta). Deploy windows: staging -> tomorrow AM.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: branch=feature/stream-client-abort-detect -> staging at 2026-03-16T03:00:00Z (CI green).

lisa_support: Assigning follow-ups: @jon_eng_runtime implement detection + metric, @kevin_sre capture pcap and confirm, @sam_billing compile req list. Customer update: sent workaround and ETA for fix (~24-48h). Will escalate if they see more failures.

maria_support: Adding tags: #streaming #billing #customer-escalation. Will post updates here when we have staging results. :thumbsup:
